posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Maybe it's a very tiny piano ;).

If you play the Adept enough, you should hopefully come to learn his deck like everyone else's - it took me a while too. There are three different songs of each type, and two copies of each song.

 

The Harmonies are…

Inspiring Supertonic (One hero use a power now/Adept regains 2hp)

Alacritous Subdominant (One hero play a card now/Adept use a power now then destroy this card)

Cedistic Dissonant (Destroy an instrument then destroy any non-character card in play/Adept discard two then draw three)

 

The Melodies are…

Rhapsody of Vigour (Up to five targets get +1hp)

Sarabande of Destruction (Destroy an ongoing or environment card)

Scherzo of Frost and Flame (Deal one target one fire damage, then deal one target one cold damage…or the other way around, I forget)

 

The Rhythms are…

Counterpoint Bulwark (Up to two targets gain +1 soak/One player draw a card now)

Syncopated Onslaught (Up to two targets gain +1 damage dealt/Deal one target one sonic damage)

Inventive Preparation (Each player may look at their top card, then either replace or discard it/One player who isn't the Adept play a card now)

 

Phew, I'm glad I was able to remember them all :). And of course, bear in mind that as mentioned above, songs are not Limited. Also, their effects aren't powers (the instruments are), so you can use a song's effect twice in a turn if you want, for example using the Harp to activate Inspiring Supertonic to let you use the Lyra to activate Inspiring Supertonic again to let you use another instrument (my usual combo once I get those cards out). The only time having two copies of the csame song out is necessary is when using the Pipes, since you can only activate two different cards with them and not the same one twice - if you have two copies of Sarabande out, you can activate both and destroy two things as a result, but if you only had one you couldn't activate it twice because the Pipes specify two different Melody cards. If one of those cards happens to look exactly the same as the other one, that's fine :).

posts.name: Spiff
posts.cooked:
Right, Spite's got that start-of-hero-turn effect.

I've attached the font (.zipped because it won't let me attach a .ttf file).  There are only a couple of letters which are active in the font:

  • uppercase H = "H" icon
  • uppercase S = "SV" icon
  • uppercase E = "EV" icon
  • lowercase s = "SH" icon
  • lowercase e = "EH" icon
  • 9 = background for rectangular end-of-turn icons
  • 0 = background for circular start-of-turn icons

Most of that should be self-explanatory, but the backgrounds work like this in Photoshop:

For an end-of-villain-turn icon, you'll type "9", then you type "E".  You'll now have a black rectangle sitting next to the "EV" icon, which is not yet what you want.  You highlight the black rectangle and change its color (red, for example), then insert the cursor between the rectangle and the "EV" and change the kerning between the two so that the "EV" moves to the left, on top of the background (I used -800 kerning).  Now what you have is an "EV" with a red background which you can copy/paste to use wherever you want, and which will stay inline with the rest of your text so you don't have to reposition images every time you move things around.  Magic!

SotM.ttf_.zip (4.03 KB)

posts.name: Spiff
posts.cooked:
I've posted the updated villain card files, and in the process decided that the way I organize my files needed to be updated as well.  Since the beginnning, I've kept file types grouped together into .zip files (all the oversized villain cards in one .zip file, all the card boxes in another, etc.).  But that means that someone who buys just a single set has to download everything I've got even though they won't use the items for expansions they don't own.  That's not great.

Now, each expansion has its own .zip file, and in that zip file are all the file types.  So, when you download the Shattered Timelines file, you'll get all the boxes, oversized cards, trackers, etc. for Shattered Timelines content and not for other stuff you don't care about.  Since all the file types are included, you'll be downloading card boxes even if all you wanted was villain cards, but I can't see a way around that.

Promos and alt cards (which have grown surprisingly bountiful over the years) have their own .zip file to keep them separate from the expansions themselves.  So forget what I said a few posts back about the Dark Watch and villain promos being in their own .zip file for now. Since promos and alts have their own home now, I've just put the new stuff in there.

www.spiffworld.com/sotm

Updates:

1) I've updated the Card List to include Andy's correct card count (thanks, Andy).

2) I've updated the FAQ to include the most recent K.N.Y.F.E. rulings.  The FAQ now also includes a copy of the Vengeance rulebook along with the Enhanced Edition rules it's always had.
